full_judgment: 5. In support of his submission Mr. Hoque has placed before me the order sheet of Partition Suit No. 67 of 1985. It appears from order No. 15 dated 11-8-86 that the summons was not as yet served upon defendant No. 2, who is the petitioner before me and 20-8-86 was fixed for service of summons upon him. It is crystal clear from this order dated 11-8-86 that defendant No. 2 was surreptitiously made defendant No. 3 subsequently in an unscrupulous zeal by defendant No. 3 by interpolation, which is easily discernible from a cursory look at the order sheet, and this fact is further magnified by order No. 16 dated 18-8-86 wherein it was specifically mentioned that the next date of the suit was fixed on 11-9-86 for service return of summons upon defendant No. 2 by usual process as well as by registered post. After that there is no order in the entire order sheet indicating that summons was ever served upon defendant No.2 in the usual course. There is also no clear proof on record to find that summons by registered post was duly served upon defendant No. 2. Although by order No.33 dated 24-5-87 the trial Court in a casual manner found that notice upon defendant No. 2 was served by registered post under the provision of section 19(b) sub-clause (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure but except this stray observation made in the order sheet there is no other material on record to prove that summons was duly served upon defendant No. 2 either by the usual process or by registered post. From this it is manifestly clear that no summons was served upon defendant No. 2 as required by law.
